conviction_note: Lean negative (p_up 44 on a 22-point absolute move scale): a ~$19m equity stub under ~$320m of debt, in a strategic review that explicitly includes recapitalisation, reports on the last legal day of its 10-Q deadline after an 11-day postponement, with FY26 operating-cash-flow guidance (0 to +$10m) needing +$8-18m in H2 after -$8.0m in H1 and no PIK capacity left; held toward 50 because the stock is already -42% in 20 sessions and -28% in 5 at a 52-week low with ~12% of float short, and Q2 bookings (+39% q/q) and five straight positive adjusted-EBITDA quarters argue the operating quarter itself may be fine. The findings sum (-4.3) is larger than the scaled number (-2.64) because the scaled number carries the squeeze and already-priced risk in p_up.

positioning_check: Short interest about 1.1-1.2m shares, ~12-13% of float, ~5.1 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (search snippets from equibles.com/stocks/stem/summary and curvedtrading.com/stocks/stem/short-interest, primary pages 403; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/STEM/sentiment shows 12.4%). Moderately crowded on 292k shares/day of average volume. No usable option chain (front-expiry ATM legs not two-sided, total OI 215, put/call OI 0.28), so there is no skew. Tape: spot $1.985, -28.1% over 5 sessions, -41.8% over 20, -90.9% from the 52-week high, at the 52-week low, 20-day realised vol 163%. Negatives below were shrunk for the short base and the drawdown.

findings.finding: Stem moved the Q3 print from 2026-11-05 to 2026-11-16 'for scheduling and logistical reasons' (release 2026-11-04), which is the last legal day for a 45-day (non-accelerated) filer's 10-Q (Sep 30 + 45 = Sat Nov 14, so Mon Nov 16). Its Q2 10-Q was accepted 2026-08-12, after the 40-day mark, so it files on the 45-day clock. The move came 9 days after the strategic review started; a print pushed to the filing deadline in a levered company under review fits extra accounting work (going-concern assessment, impairment testing, subsequent-events disclosure). The market reads this as a neutral reschedule.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior delayed print in the baseline. The last two prints went -19.98% (2026-05-06) and +21.19% (2026-03-04); the 2025-10-29 Q3 print went -26.67%.
findings.why_not_priced: The only coverage, a German market note (goldesel.de), says the logistical reason by itself signals no change in conditions. Nobody has tied the new date to the 10-Q deadline. If the market had, it would be looking for an NT 10-Q or going-concern language. Instead the stock bounced +15.6% on 2026-11-06, two days after the reschedule.
findings.independence: Inference from the timing. The 10-Q filing clock comes from the EDGAR submissions list (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001758766.json: 10-Q accepted 2026-08-12T23:18Z). Goldesel (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/stem-inc-a-aktie-stem-verschiebt-q3-zahlen-auf-den-16-november) reads it the other way, as neutral.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-26 the board began a formal strategic review with Guggenheim Securities and with Gibson Dunn and Davis Polk as counsel. Options explicitly include refinancing and recapitalization as well as a sale. The review sits on ~$19m of equity value (9.63m shares at 2026-08-05 times $1.985) against $118.7m of 4.25% 2030 converts plus ~$135m carrying (~$160m face) of 11% senior secured notes, and a stockholders' deficit of $(270)m. Any recap or sale path the call characterizes likely ranks common equity last. The company said it will not update on the review until a transaction is approved, so the call is the first time management speaks since the review began.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement itself took the stock down ~13% on 2026-10-27 on ~5x volume (https://stockstotrade.com/news/stem-inc-class-a-stem-news-2026-10-27/). It has kept falling since: $2.25-3.00 then, $1.985 now.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is down ~40% since the announcement. What is not priced is the call's framing. A 'recapitalization' emphasis, or equity raised or exchanged in the 10-Q subsequent-events note, would reprice the stub. If the market had fully priced a wipe-out, the equity would trade at option value well under $1.
findings.independence: Debt figures come from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001758766/000175876626000078/exhibit99-8xkx20260812xq22.htm). A commentary piece (https://briefglance.com/articles/stems-strategic-review-signals-a-clean-tech-software-reckoning, 2026-10-26) puts the senior secured notes at $160m face and market cap at ~$33.5m on the review date. Its list of possible buyers is speculation and was not used.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide is under strain on cash rather than revenue. Operating-cash-flow guidance of $0-10m needs +$8m to +$18m in H2 after -$8.0m in H1, and the 10-Q says there is no remaining capacity to pay senior-secured interest in kind, so 11% cash interest on ~$160m (~$8-9m a half) now runs through OCF. Revenue of $140-190m needs $77-127m in H2 against $62.7m in H1; FY consensus of $147.4m already sits near the low end. During a strategic review a guide cut or withdrawal on OCF, EBITDA or ARR ($65-70m year-end vs $62.4m at Q2) is the likeliest guidance event.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide was reaffirmed on the 2026-05-06 print (-19.98%) and the 2026-08-12 Q2 print. A 2024 guide cut with a strategic review was a large negative for this name (energy-storage.news headline, URL date unverified; see rejected_candidates).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sell-side has trimmed targets and FY revenue consensus sits at the bottom of the range. OCF, the guide line that looks hardest to hit, does not appear in any aggregator consensus. If it were priced, an OCF or ARR guide cut would read as a non-event, and the stock would not have bounced 15.6% on 2026-11-06.
findings.independence: The no-remaining-PIK statement is in the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001758766/000175876626000081/stem-20260630.htm), the same filing family as the release. FY consensus comes from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/stem/forecast/. Shares the Q2 filing with finding 4.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q's liquidity footing is thin and goes to the 10-Q due today: $38.4m cash, negative working capital of $18.2m, $1.52bn accumulated deficit. Management stated cash is sufficient for 12 months but 'may need additional equity or debt financing'. The $30m Jefferies ATM ($24.2m left at 6/30, 595k shares sold in Q2 for $5.6m net) is of limited use at a ~$19m market cap. Q3 cash, any ATM dilution, and whether the 12-month sufficiency language survives or turns into going-concern doubt all land in the release and 10-Q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior going-concern flag. Cash fell from $48.9m (Dec-25) to $36.6m (Mar-26), then rose to $38.4m (Jun-26) with ATM help.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q2 language said 12 months was covered, so a change to going-concern doubt would be new. The financing here buys runway rather than a ramp: bookings rose but no backlog build is disclosed that the cash funds. If the market had priced a going-concern flag, the 2026-11-06 +15.6% bounce and the UBS Buy upgrade of 2026-09-28 would not sit in the record.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 filing with finding 3; this finding covers the liquidity disclosure, finding 3 the guide arithmetic. A secondary write-up (https://www.panabee.com/news/stem-earnings-q2-2026-report, AI-generated, 2026-08-12) also flags liquidity as the main risk.

findings.finding: Q2 operating momentum argues the reported quarter can meet or beat a disputed $37-40m revenue bar. Q2 bookings were $36.8m, +39% q/q from $26.5m. ARR rose to $62.4m from $61.2m. GAAP gross margin was 41% (33% a year earlier). Adj. EBITDA was $6.2m, the fifth straight positive quarter. OCF turned +$0.3m in Q2 after -$8.3m in Q1. Q3 2025 revenue was $38.2m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has sold good quarters before. After the Q2 2026 print (positive EBITDA, guide reaffirmed) the stock kept falling into Q3; 4 of the last 6 reactions were up and the median absolute move is 20.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: At an equity stub priced for distress, a clean operating quarter with stable cash would not be in the price. A stock pricing an in-line quarter would not have fallen 28% in the five sessions before the print.
findings.independence: Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001758766/000175876626000043/exhibit99-8xkx20260506xq12.htm) gives the bookings and EBITDA trajectory. UBS upgraded to Buy with a $7 target on 2026-09-28 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/stem/forecast/).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is stretched: -28.1% over 5 sessions and -41.8% over 20, at the 52-week low, with ~12% of float short (~5 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement) and 163% realised vol. Any print short of a going-concern flag or a dilutive recap could squeeze.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +15.6% on 2026-11-06 with no company news after the reschedule. The 2026-03-04 print went +21.19% after a drawdown.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself. The finding is that the short base is a mechanism against further downside, not that something is unpriced. No cause for the last five sessions' drop was found.
findings.independence: The tape figures come from the sealed baseline (Yahoo daily bars). Short-interest snippets from equibles and curvedtrading broadly agree (12-13% of float).

findings.finding: Sell-side cut targets into the quarter: Susquehanna to $4.50 from $7.50 on 2026-10-14 (Neutral), and BMO to $5 from $8 on 2026-10-21 (Hold). That lowers the bar and reflects deteriorating estimates before the review was announced.
findings.why_not_priced: This is wire copy and is priced; filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: NYSE 802.01B non-compliance: average market cap below $50m over 30 trading days and stockholders' equity below $50m (letter received 2026-10-20). The business plan is due within 45 days, around 2026-12-04. Separately, under 802.01B a 30-trading-day average global market cap below $15m means prompt suspension and delisting with no cure. At $1.985 times ~9.6m+ shares the cap is ~$19m, so a post-print drop of ~25% sustained for weeks would cross it. Neither event resolves inside the window.

Cash interest on the 11% senior secured notes now has no PIK capacity left (Q2 10-Q). The semi-annual payment date is not verified; it is likely around 2026-12-01, given the 2030-12-01 maturity, and falls after the window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (unusable chain). The negative lean goes with a -42% 20-day run-up, which means much of it is already in the price, and against a ~12%-of-float short base; both moved p_up from 42 to 44.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar: Benzinga $39.7m vs EW $37.2m): the reported-quarter momentum finding was capped from +1.5 to +1.0 and print_vs_bar moved from -3 to -2.
Rule 5 (an unexplained microcap drawdown is worth 0; documents beat inference): the positioning finding went from +2.0 to +1.0, and the reschedule-timing inference from -2.0 to -1.5.
Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives) and the core's priced-wire-copy row: the strategic review went from -2.0 to -1.5, analyst target cuts from -0.5 to -0.3, and p_up from 42 to 44.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the Q2 10-Q carries no going-concern flag and the money buys runway, not a ramp, so the liquidity finding was kept negative but cut from -1.5 to -1.0.
Rule 6 window: the NYSE $15m/plan deadline and the December interest date stay in outside_window.
Rule 8: abs_move_pct kept at 22, not shrunk.
